name: Alpha-Ketoglutarate (AKG)
summary: Alpha-ketoglutarate is an endogenous tricarboxylic-acid-cycle intermediate and co-substrate for multiple dioxygenase enzymes. It is marketed in longevity and healthy-aging products, but direct randomized human evidence for lifespan or broad anti-aging claims remains limited; widely cited biological-age findings include uncontrolled or multi-ingredient evidence that cannot establish a causal AKG effect. This profile remains research-only.
description: Canonical alpha-ketoglutarate research entity for evidence integration. Publication remains held while mechanistic, clinical, formulation-specific, and longevity claims are separated and the human intervention evidence is systematically reviewed.
primary_effects_or_targets: TCA-cycle metabolism; dioxygenase co-substrate activity; nitrogen metabolism; healthy-aging research
